newsitem.title: USA: General Instrument restructuring set for July 28.
newsitem.headline: General Instrument restructuring set for July 28.

text.p: General Instrument Corp said Wednesday it expects to complete on July 28 a strategic restructuring plan to separate into three independent public companies: NextLevel Systems Inc, CommScope Inc, and General Semiconductor Inc.

Subject to final approval by stockholders at a combined annual and special meeting on July 23, 1997, General Instrument plans to complete the restructuring through a tax-free distribution to stockholders.

All General Instrument stockholders of record on July 25, 1997, will receive shares of NextLevel Systems (one share for each GI share held) and CommScope (one share for every three GI shares held) prior to the opening of business on July 28.
Also prior to the opening of business on July 28, General Instrument will change its name to General Semiconductor Inc and effect a one-for-four reverse stock split.

Pending completion of the distributions, the three companies have been approved for listing on the New York Stock Exchange, with the following ticker symbols: NextLevel Systems (NLV), CommScope (CTV), and General Semiconductor (SEM).

NextLevel Systems, with operations in Pennsylvania and California, supplies systems and components for high-performance networks delivering video, voice and Internet/data services. CommScope is the world's largest manufacturer of coaxial cable. General Semiconductor Inc (currently Power Semiconductor) sells semiconductors.
